page: OVHcloud c2-7 is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel processor from the Haswell microarchitecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs, providing a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It includes 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.5 GB of RAM per core, alongside a bundled 50 GB local SSD for storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2-7 demonstrates entry-level performance characteristics. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 10% of benchmarked hardware, with scores of 864.27 and 1718.26 respectively. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read-only bandwidth measured at 20.03 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 16.03 GB/sec. However, the server achieves an average tier result in LLM text generation using a small 135M model, reaching 74.86 tokens per second, though prompt processing remains in the weak category at 212.61 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2-7 offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated compute resources, avoiding the performance fluctuations associated with shared-core or burstable instances. However, the older Intel Haswell architecture and lower memory bandwidth present clear tradeoffs for modern, resource-intensive applications. This instance is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale database operations, simple text processing, or running utility scripts that require dedicated CPU allocation without high memory or I/O demands.
